'''Don Mottram''' (born 1945 in [[Cheshire]]) is a retired [[England|English]] [[Flavour (taste)|flavour]] [[chemist]] based at the [[Department of Food and Nutritional Sciences]] of the [[University of Reading]].

Having obtained an [[honours degree]] in [[colour]] [[chemistry]] from the [[University of Leeds]] in 1967 he spent a year working as a volunteer with [[Voluntary Service Overseas]] in [[Dacca]], [[Bangladesh]] (formerly [[East Pakistan]]) before returning to [[Leeds]] to study for a Ph.D. in [[colour]] [[chemistry]]. Following his graduation in 1971, Mottram took up a post at the [[Meat Research Institute]] at [[Lower Langford|Langford]], near [[Bristol]], [[United Kingdom|UK]].

Mottram moved to the [[University of Reading]] in 1988. His research interests are mainly in the area of [[Flavour (taste)|flavour]] [[chemistry]], the [[Chemical analysis|analysis]] of [[Flavour (taste)|flavour]] and the factors affecting its formation and retention in foods, especially [[meat]].

Following the detection of the potential [[carcinogen]] [[acrylamide]] in a range of fried and oven-cooked foods, Mottram, in collaboration with Professor [[Bronek Wedzicha]] of the [[University of Leeds]], provided an important breakthrough in understanding the origin of [[acrylamide]] in cooked foods which was published in ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]''.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Mottram |first=Donald S. |last2=Wedzicha |first2=Bronislaw L. |last3=Dodson |first3=Andrew T. |date=October 2002 |title=Acrylamide is formed in the Maillard reaction |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/419448a |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=419 |issue=6906 |pages=448–449 |doi=10.1038/419448a |issn=1476-4687|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Mottram also collaborated with [[chef]] [[Heston Blumenthal]] of [[The Fat Duck]] [[restaurant]] in the village of [[Bray, Berkshire|Bray]] in [[Berkshire]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kirsty |date=2017-01-20 |title=Chemistry is like cooking - just don't lick the spoon! - Asynt |url=https://www.asynt.com/blog/chemistry-like-cooking-just-dont-lick-spoon/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250207023334/https://www.asynt.com/blog/chemistry-like-cooking-just-dont-lick-spoon/ |archive-date=2025-02-07 |access-date=2026-08-12 |work=Asynt |language=en-GB}}</ref>
